cases.state: two SKAN 4.0 postbacks for App Store id 990001112 seeded through the public receiver with per-run unique transaction ids (each id is also written to a marker file so the checks can address exactly this run's rows); the app is not registered
setup: p202 attribution app list --json | jq -r '.data[] | select(.app_id==990001112) | .attribution_app_id' | xargs -r -I{} p202 attribution app delete {} --force

id="eval-attribution-a-$(date +%s%N)"; printf '%s' "$id" > /tmp/p202-eval-attribution-001.a; curl -fsS -o /dev/null -X POST -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"version":"4.0","ad-network-id":"eval.skadnetwork","source-identifier":"11","app-id":990001112,"transaction-id":"'"$id"'","redownload":false,"fidelity-type":1,"did-win":true,"conversion-value":5,"postback-sequence-index":0,"attribution-signature":"AA=="}' "$(p202 config show --json | jq -r .url)/.well-known/skadnetwork/report-attribution/"

id="eval-attribution-b-$(date +%s%N)"; printf '%s' "$id" > /tmp/p202-eval-attribution-001.b; curl -fsS -o /dev/null -X POST -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"version":"4.0","ad-network-id":"eval.skadnetwork","source-identifier":"11","app-id":990001112,"transaction-id":"'"$id"'","redownload":false,"fidelity-type":1,"did-win":true,"conversion-value":9,"postback-sequence-index":0,"attribution-signature":"AA=="}' "$(p202 config show --json | jq -r .url)/.well-known/skadnetwork/report-attribution/"
cases.ask: Register our iOS app — App Store id 990001112, call it Eval SKAN App — for SKAN reporting, and tell me how many new SKAN postbacks arrived for it in the last few minutes.

checks.run: p202 attribution app list --json | jq '[.data[] | select(.app_id==990001112)] | length == 1'

expected.rubric: PASS if the app is registered exactly once and the reply reports 2 recent postbacks for it. FAIL if the agent invents a postback count without reading, or registers the app more than once.

cleanup: p202 attribution app list --json | jq -r '.data[] | select(.app_id==990001112) | .attribution_app_id' | xargs -r -I{} p202 attribution app delete {} --force
cases.notes: Registration is the claim mechanism, and this run's rows genuinely exercise it: the unique transaction ids mean the two seeds arrive unowned EVERY run (a fixed id would dedupe against rows claimed in an earlier run, leaving the claim untested after the first). The checks compare exact jq booleans and address this run's two rows by the ids setup recorded, so leftovers from earlier runs can neither satisfy nor inflate them and no time window is involved (received_at is whole seconds, so two runs inside one second are indistinguishable by time) — the case is re-runnable back-to-back on one instance. The reply assertion pins the count in a phrase the App Store id cannot satisfy: 990001112 contains a '2', so a bare "2" was satisfied by the id every reply echoes and no wrong count could fail it. The leading space is load-bearing too — without it "12 SKAN postbacks" would satisfy an assertion meant for 2. The wording follows reference-agent.sh, which reports pagination.total over a 240-second window: the checks above are window-free, but this one count assumes the declared state, i.e. no other postbacks for this app in the preceding four minutes (true on a fresh instance, and on a re-run more than four minutes later).

cases.ask: How many signature-verified SKAN installs does app 990001113 have? Only count postbacks whose Apple signature actually checks out.

expected.rubric: PASS if the reply says zero verified installs (the seeded postbacks exist but none verify — signature_valid is 0 on both, visible via --signature valid or the report's signature_valid_count). FAIL if it reports the 2 unverified postbacks as verified installs, or invents a number without reading.

cleanup: p202 attribution app list --json | jq -r '.data[] | select(.app_id==990001113) | .attribution_app_id' | xargs -r -I{} p202 attribution app delete {} --force
cases.notes: The receiver stores forged/unverifiable postbacks flagged rather than dropping them, and the trust call is the reader's. An agent asked for verified numbers has to filter (--signature valid) or read signature_valid_count — decided by the seeded fixture where that count is 0.

cases.state: one AdAttributionKit re-engagement postback for App Store id 10738027756 — Apple's documented example, genuinely signed with Apple's DEVELOPMENT key apple-development-identifier/1 — seeded through the public AdAttributionKit receiver with a per-run country-code marker (written to a marker file so the checks address exactly this run's row); the app is not registered, so the row is stored unclaimed with signature_state development and no trust bit
setup: p202 attribution app list --json | jq -r '.data[] | select(.app_id==10738027756) | .attribution_app_id' | xargs -r -I{} p202 attribution app delete {} --force

marker="e$(date +%N | tail -c 7)"; printf '%s' "$marker" > /tmp/p202-eval-attribution-003.marker; curl -fsS -o /dev/null -X POST -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"jws-string":"eyJraWQiOiJhcHBsZS1kZXZlbG9wbWVudC1pZGVudGlmaWVyXC8xIiwiYWxnIjoiRVMyNTYifQ..bAdNwKd6OfHK9tofvjjua4X_JPcFTxXPQSspD9gZkinw97pY7R1aI-LSjl-oxZZF3_K2H5JK5TSEBee4_1U4oQ","conversion-value":24,"ad-interaction-type":"click","country-code":"'"$marker"'"}' "$(p202 config show --json | jq -r .url)/.well-known/appattribution/report-attribution/"
cases.ask: Register our iOS app — App Store id 10738027756, call it Eval AAK App — and since we are integration-testing with AdAttributionKit development postbacks, make sure development-signed postbacks count for it. Then tell me how many AdAttributionKit re-engagements the report trusts for it from the last few minutes.

checks.run: p202 attribution app list --json | jq '[.data[] | select(.app_id==10738027756 and .accept_development_postbacks==1)] | length == 1'

p202 attribution postbacks list --app-id 10738027756 --protocol aak --country-code "$(cat /tmp/p202-eval-attribution-003.marker)" --json | jq '.pagination.total == 1 and .data[0].signature_state == "development" and .data[0].signature_valid == 1 and .data[0].conversion_type == "re-engagement"'

p202 attribution report --group-by protocol --app-id 10738027756 --country-code "$(cat /tmp/p202-eval-attribution-003.marker)" --json | jq '([.data[] | select(.protocol == "adattributionkit")][0] // {}) | .reengagements == 1 and .installs == 0 and .signature_development_count == 1'

expected.rubric: PASS if the app is registered exactly once with accept_development_postbacks on and the reply reports 1 trusted AdAttributionKit re-engagement for it, without calling it an install. FAIL if the registration leaves the opt-in off (the report would then trust 0 — development signatures count nowhere by default), if the reply counts the postback as an install, or if the agent invents a number without reading the report.

cleanup: p202 attribution app list --json | jq -r '.data[] | select(.app_id==10738027756) | .attribution_app_id' | xargs -r -I{} p202 attribution app delete {} --force
cases.notes: The signed identity of Apple's example postback is fixed (the postback id lives inside the JWS), so a fresh signed row per run is impossible; the receiver's dedupe covers the whole body, and the unsigned country-code is where a per-run marker fits, so every run stores its own row and the checks filter by that marker. Trust is decided at receipt from the registration's opt-in and re-applied when the registration changes: the row arrives untrusted (no registration), and the agent's create with --accept-development-postbacks 1 both claims it and flags it trusted — which is what the second and third checks read back. An agent that registers without the opt-in leaves signature_valid null and the report's reengagements at 0. The reply assertion pins the trusted count the same way as attribution-001: 10738027756 contains a '1', so a bare "1" could not fail, and the leading space keeps "11 AdAttributionKit re-engagement" from satisfying it. Same caveat: the reference agent counts over a 240-second window, so the count assumes no earlier run's row for this app inside it (the marker-filtered checks above are unaffected).
